headline: Metro Manila Minimum Wage to Rise by ₱60 on September 26 Under New NCR Order
seoTitle: Metro Manila Minimum Wage Rises by ₱60 on Sept. 26 | FMB News
seoDescription: DOLE says Wage Order NCR-28 will raise Metro Manila daily minimum wages by ₱60 effective September 26, 2026, while the earlier NCR-27 order remains tied to litigation.
deck: DOLE says Wage Order NCR-28 will take effect on September 26, raising the daily minimum wage in Metro Manila by ₱60 while the earlier ₱85 order remains under court dispute.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Minimum-wage workers in Metro Manila are set to receive a ₱60 daily increase starting September 26, 2026, under Wage Order NCR-28, according to the Department of Labor and Employment.

DOLE said the new order raises the daily minimum wage for non-agricultural workers from ₱695 to ₱755. For workers in agriculture, service and retail establishments with 15 or fewer workers, and manufacturing establishments regularly employing fewer than 10 workers, the rate rises from ₱658 to ₱718.

The order is separate from Wage Order NCR-27, the earlier ₱85 increase that became the subject of court proceedings. FMB News is treating the new order as its own verified administrative action and is not assuming that the litigation over NCR-27 has been resolved.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board-National Capital Region approved the fresh ₱60 increase after implementation of Wage Order NCR-27 became entangled in litigation.
Philippine News Agency and ABS-CBN News separately reported the approval of the new ₱60 order, while BusinessWorld reported that the fresh order was issued amid the continuing dispute over NCR-27.

DOLE's current official release states that Wage Order NCR-28 takes effect on September 26, 2026. That official effectivity statement resolves an earlier verification gap over whether the new order had completed the steps needed for implementation.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The change directly affects covered minimum-wage workers and employers across Metro Manila. A ₱60 increase changes base daily pay and can also affect calculations tied to wage rates, including certain overtime and premium-pay amounts under applicable labor rules.

For households, the increase provides additional nominal income at a time of elevated fuel, transport and other living costs. For businesses, especially smaller employers, it raises labor costs and may require payroll adjustments before the September 26 effectivity date.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for formal implementation guidance from DOLE and the NCR wage board, employer compliance, any new legal challenge involving NCR-28, and developments in the separate case involving Wage Order NCR-27.
Workers should also watch for official advisories explaining exemptions, coverage and wage-distortion issues where applicable rather than relying on social-media summaries.

verificationNotes: DOLE is the primary source for the central claim and currently states that Wage Order NCR-28 takes effect on September 26, 2026.
PNA and ABS-CBN News independently corroborate the approval of the fresh ₱60 wage order.
BusinessWorld independently reported the new order in the context of the unresolved dispute involving Wage Order NCR-27.
The article does not state that litigation over NCR-27 has been resolved. The two wage orders are clearly distinguished.
No prior FMB News article matching Wage Order NCR-28 was found in the canonical repository search before publication.
